---
title: "Kaveri catchment rainfall"
output: html_notebook
---

```{r}
require(tidyverse)
require(arrow)
require(lubridate)
require(trend)
require(ggrepel)
```

What exactly are we measuring?

- A year means a calendar year. We can add the June-May water year later.
- "Rainfall in the catchment" means area-weighted rainfall depth in mm. It is
  also converted to km3 falling over that area. It is not reservoir inflow.
- The CWC boundary defines the whole basin. HydroBASINS topology defines land
  upstream of each dam or gauge, so tributaries are included automatically.
- The main trend window is 1951-2024. The early IMD grid has a large pre-1951
  break in the Kabini/Western Ghats cells; 2025 is provisional.

First look at the geography and the cells.

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/kaveri_catchment_map.png")
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/kaveri_imd_cells_map.png")
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/kaveri_checkpoint_zones.png")
```

```{r}
zone_summary <- read_csv(
  "data/kaveri_zone_summary.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

monthly <- read_parquet("data/kaveri_rainfall_monthly.parquet")
annual <- read_parquet("data/kaveri_rainfall_annual.parquet")

zone_summary %>%
  select(zone, zone_area_km2, cells, grid_coverage_pct)
```

The whole CWC basin uses 153 IMD cells and has 99.4% grid-area coverage. All
checkpoint catchments have effectively complete coverage. Every annual row has
12 months and either 365 or 366 observed days.

## Has rainfall shifted since 1951?

```{r}
zone_order <- c(
  "whole_basin",
  "within_karnataka",
  "upstream_krs",
  "upstream_harangi",
  "upstream_hemavathi",
  "upstream_kabini",
  "upstream_biligundlu",
  "upstream_mettur",
  "upstream_bhavanisagar",
  "upstream_amaravathi"
)

zone_labels <- c(
  whole_basin = "Whole basin",
  within_karnataka = "Within Karnataka",
  upstream_krs = "Upstream of KRS",
  upstream_harangi = "Upstream of Harangi",
  upstream_hemavathi = "Upstream of Hemavathi",
  upstream_kabini = "Upstream of Kabini",
  upstream_biligundlu = "Upstream of Biligundlu",
  upstream_mettur = "Upstream of Mettur",
  upstream_bhavanisagar = "Upstream of Bhavanisagar",
  upstream_amaravathi = "Upstream of Amaravathi"
)

trend_stats <- annual %>%
  filter(year >= 1951, year <= 2024) %>%
  group_by(zone_id, zone) %>%
  group_modify(function(d, key) {
    sen <- trend::sens.slope(d$rainfall_mm)
    mk <- trend::mk.test(d$rainfall_mm)

    tibble(
      mean_mm = mean(d$rainfall_mm),
      sd_mm = sd(d$rainfall_mm),
      cv = sd_mm / mean_mm,
      sen_mm_decade = unname(sen$estimates) * 10,
      mann_kendall_p = mk$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

period_change <- annual %>%
  filter(year %in% c(1951:1980, 1995:2024)) %>%
  mutate(period = if_else(year <= 1980, "1951-1980", "1995-2024")) %>%
  summarise(period_mean_mm = mean(rainfall_mm), .by = c(zone_id, period)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = period, values_from = period_mean_mm) %>%
  mutate(
    change_mm = `1995-2024` - `1951-1980`,
    change_pct = 100 * change_mm / `1951-1980`
  )

trend_summary <- trend_stats %>%
  left_join(period_change, by = "zone_id") %>%
  mutate(
    zone_short = unname(zone_labels[zone_id]),
    zone_id = factor(zone_id, levels = zone_order)
  ) %>%
  arrange(zone_id)

trend_summary %>%
  transmute(
    zone = zone_short,
    mean_mm = round(mean_mm),
    sen_mm_decade = round(sen_mm_decade, 1),
    mann_kendall_p = round(mann_kendall_p, 3),
    recent_vs_early_pct = round(change_pct, 1)
  )
```

```{r}
write_csv(
  trend_summary %>%
    select(
      zone_id, zone_short, mean_mm, sd_mm, cv,
      sen_mm_decade, mann_kendall_p,
      `1951-1980`, `1995-2024`, change_mm, change_pct
    ),
  "data/kaveri_trend_summary.csv"
)
```

The whole basin's recent 30-year average is 5% above 1951-80. That average
hides a split: KRS and Karnataka are about 12% higher, while Bhavanisagar is
13% lower and Kabini 7% lower.

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
annual_plot <- annual %>%
  filter(year >= 1951) %>%
  mutate(
    zone_short = unname(zone_labels[zone_id]),
    zone_id = factor(zone_id, levels = zone_order)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    trend_summary %>%
      transmute(
        zone_id,
        facet_label = paste0(
          zone_short,
          " · ",
          scales::number(change_pct, accuracy = 0.1, scale_cut = NULL, prefix = if_else(change_pct > 0, "+", "")),
          "% recent vs early"
        )
      ),
    by = "zone_id"
  ) %>%
  arrange(zone_id, year) %>%
  group_by(zone_id, facet_label) %>%
  mutate(
    rolling_11yr = as.numeric(
      stats::filter(rainfall_mm, rep(1 / 11, 11), sides = 1)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    facet_label = factor(
      facet_label,
      levels = trend_summary %>%
        transmute(
          label = paste0(
            zone_short,
            " · ",
            scales::number(change_pct, accuracy = 0.1, scale_cut = NULL, prefix = if_else(change_pct > 0, "+", "")),
            "% recent vs early"
          )
        ) %>%
        pull(label)
    )
  )

annual_plot %>%
  filter(year <= 2024) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, rainfall_mm)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey72", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_point(colour = "grey48", size = 0.65) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = rolling_11yr),
    colour = "#176d6e",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = annual_plot %>% filter(year == 2025),
    shape = 21,
    fill = "white",
    colour = "#a65425",
    size = 2,
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label), ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1960, 2020, 20)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "Kaveri rainfall has edged up, but its tributaries diverge",
    subtitle = "Annual totals and trailing 11-year means, 1951-2024. Panel scales vary; open point is provisional 2025.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "annual rainfall (mm)",
    caption = "Recent vs early compares 1995-2024 with 1951-1980. Rainfall is area-weighted over each catchment; it is not river inflow. Source: IMD 0.25° daily grid."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", hjust = 0, size = 7.5),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 12)
  ) -> annual_chart

ggsave(
  "outputs/kaveri_annual_rainfall_trends.png",
  annual_chart,
  width = 10,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 180,
  bg = "white"
)
```

The same result is easier to compare as one ranked change chart.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
trend_summary %>%
  mutate(
    zone_short = fct_reorder(zone_short, change_pct),
    direction = if_else(change_pct >= 0, "higher", "lower"),
    label = paste0(
      if_else(change_pct > 0, "+", ""),
      round(change_pct, 1),
      "%"
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(change_pct, zone_short, fill = direction)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = label,
      hjust = if_else(change_pct >= 0, -0.15, 1.15)
    ),
    colour = "grey15",
    size = 3.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(higher = "#176d6e", lower = "#bd7b55"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    limits = c(-16, 17),
    breaks = seq(-15, 15, 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Recent rainfall is higher around KRS, lower in Bhavani and Kabini",
    subtitle = "Difference between the 1995-2024 and 1951-1980 annual averages",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Descriptive period comparison, not a causal or runoff estimate. Source: IMD 0.25° daily grid; area-weighted to CWC/HydroBASINS catchments."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "grey20"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", hjust = 0, size = 7.5),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 28, 12, 12)
  ) -> change_chart

ggsave(
  "outputs/kaveri_recent_vs_early_rainfall.png",
  change_chart,
  width = 9,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 180,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## When does each part get its rain?

```{r}
monthly_volume <- monthly %>%
  filter(year >= 1951, year <= 2024) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_km3 = mean(rainfall_km3),
    .by = c(zone_id, zone, month)
  ) %>%
  group_by(zone_id) %>%
  mutate(
    annual_mean_km3 = sum(mean_km3),
    peak = mean_km3 == max(mean_km3),
    zone_short = unname(zone_labels[zone_id])
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    zone_id = factor(zone_id, levels = zone_order),
    month_label = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb)
  )
```

Rainfall depth is useful for comparing how wet two catchments are. It is not
additive. For cumulative checkpoints, use the total volume of rain falling over
the upstream area.

```{r}
mainstem_order <- c(
  "upstream_krs",
  "upstream_biligundlu",
  "upstream_mettur",
  "whole_basin"
)

mainstem_summary <- monthly_volume %>%
  filter(as.character(zone_id) %in% mainstem_order) %>%
  distinct(zone_id, zone_short, annual_mean_km3) %>%
  mutate(zone_id = factor(as.character(zone_id), levels = mainstem_order)) %>%
  arrange(zone_id)

mainstem_summary %>%
  transmute(
    checkpoint = zone_short,
    gross_rainfall_km3_year = round(annual_mean_km3, 1)
  )
```

The cumulative main-stem sequence now behaves as it should: about 11.9 km³ of
rain falls upstream of KRS each year, rising to 35.8 at Biligundlu, 40.5 at
Mettur, and 81.7 across the whole basin.

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
mainstem_monthly <- monthly_volume %>%
  filter(as.character(zone_id) %in% mainstem_order) %>%
  mutate(
    zone_id = factor(as.character(zone_id), levels = mainstem_order),
    series_label = paste0(
      zone_short,
      " · ",
      round(annual_mean_km3, 1),
      " km³/year"
    )
  )

mainstem_endpoints <- mainstem_monthly %>%
  filter(month == 12)

mainstem_monthly %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, mean_km3, colour = zone_id, group = zone_id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 1.7) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = mainstem_endpoints,
    aes(label = series_label),
    direction = "y",
    hjust = 0,
    nudge_x = 0.45,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    segment.colour = "grey65",
    segment.size = 0.25,
    size = 3.1,
    seed = 42,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("#9cbcbc", "#679b99", "#397f7d", "#175f60"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10, 12),
    labels = month.abb[c(1, 4, 7, 10, 12)],
    limits = c(1, 14.8)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Rainfall volume accumulates downstream",
    subtitle = "Average gross rainfall over nested upstream areas, 1951-2024",
    x = NULL,
    y = "mean monthly rainfall volume (km³)",
    caption = "KRS → Biligundlu → Mettur are cumulative main-stem checkpoints. Volume is rainfall over land, not reservoir inflow. Source: IMD 0.25° daily grid."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", hjust = 0, size = 7.5),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 110, 12, 12)
  ) -> mainstem_monthly_chart

ggsave(
  "outputs/kaveri_monthly_rainfall_climatology.png",
  mainstem_monthly_chart,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 180,
  bg = "white"
)
```

Harangi, Hemavathi, Kabini, Bhavanisagar and Amaravathi are tributary branches,
not successive downstream checkpoints. Their volumes should be read separately.

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.5}
tributary_order <- c(
  "upstream_harangi",
  "upstream_hemavathi",
  "upstream_kabini",
  "upstream_bhavanisagar",
  "upstream_amaravathi"
)

tributary_monthly <- monthly_volume %>%
  filter(as.character(zone_id) %in% tributary_order) %>%
  mutate(
    zone_id = factor(as.character(zone_id), levels = tributary_order),
    facet_label = paste0(
      zone_short,
      " · ",
      round(annual_mean_km3, 1),
      " km³/year"
    )
  )

tributary_facet_levels <- tributary_monthly %>%
  distinct(zone_id, facet_label) %>%
  arrange(zone_id) %>%
  pull(facet_label)

tributary_monthly <- tributary_monthly %>%
  mutate(
    facet_label = factor(
      facet_label,
      levels = tributary_facet_levels
    )
  )

tributary_monthly %>%
  ggplot(aes(month_label, mean_km3, fill = peak)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  facet_wrap(vars(facet_label), ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "grey78", `TRUE` = "#176d6e"),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = month.abb[c(1, 4, 7, 10)]) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Tributary reservoirs sit on separate branches",
    subtitle = "Average monthly gross rainfall over each upstream catchment, 1951-2024; shared scale",
    x = NULL,
    y = "mean monthly rainfall volume (km³)",
    caption = "Peak month highlighted. These five catchments are not a downstream sequence. Source: IMD 0.25° daily grid."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey45", hjust = 0, size = 7.5),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 12)
  ) -> tributary_monthly_chart

ggsave(
  "outputs/kaveri_tributary_monthly_rainfall.png",
  tributary_monthly_chart,
  width = 10,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 180,
  bg = "white"
)
```

What this still does not answer: how much reaches a reservoir. That needs
runoff, evapotranspiration, soil storage, withdrawals, and reservoir operations.
